article_title: Developing Educational Leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy
citation: Fitz, J., Levin, S., & Wechsler, M. E. (2024). Developing educational leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/515.306
title: 21st Century California School Leadership Academy (21CSLA)
description: 21CSLA is a statewide California initiative providing "high-quality professional learning opportunities that are accessible and free of charge to California's PreK–12 educational leaders," including central office, site, and teacher leaders. It is administered by a State Center at UC Berkeley in partnership with UCLA and the California Subject Matter Project, and delivers learning through seven regional academies as a lead agency in California's Statewide System of Support.
requirements: Regional academy offerings must align with the California Professional Standards for Education Leaders and the Quality Professional Learning Standards
constraints: Participation is open to leaders from schools and districts that receive federal Title II funds
target_learners: PreK–12 central office leaders, site leaders, and teacher leaders, with special focus on novice leaders, leaders in high-need settings, and leaders involved in school improvement
examples: In the first grant cycle the initiative served approximately 8,300 leaders and its deliverables required at least 12 hours for communities of practice and localized offerings and a minimum of 25 hours of individual coaching
key_sources: Fitz, J., Levin, S., & Wechsler, M. E. (2024). Developing educational leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/515.306

article_title: Developing Educational Leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy
citation: Fitz, J., Levin, S., & Wechsler, M. E. (2024). Developing educational leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/515.306
title: Three synergistic professional learning modalities: communities of practice, localized professional learning, and coaching
description: 21CSLA regional academies deliver professional learning through three primary modalities. According to the report, "Communities of practice allow leaders to participate in collaborative learning. Localized professional learning provides experiences that are problem based and context specific. Coaching enables individualized, tailored support and opportunities for feedback and reflection." The State Center's guidance describes the three modalities as synergistic and complementary, and all activities must occur over an extended duration.
requirements: Communities of practice and localized offerings must involve at least 12 hours of professional learning; coaching must provide a minimum of 25 hours of individual leadership coaching per participant
constraints: Regional academies have flexibility in delivery and content, but implementation is structured by the State Center's guidance document
target_learners: school administrators, teacher leaders, and district administrators in California
examples: Year 3 deliverables required a minimum of 12 communities of practice groups, eight localized learning opportunities serving at least 240 participants, and coaching for a minimum of 60 leaders
key_sources: Fitz, J., Levin, S., & Wechsler, M. E. (2024). Developing educational leaders in California: The 21st Century California School Leadership Academy. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/515.306

article_title: Integrating 21st Century Skills into Teaching English: Investigating Its Effect on Listening and Speaking Skills
citation: Hamid Ashraf, Fatemeh Ahmadi, Mansooreh Hosseinnia. (2017). Integrating 21st Century Skills into Teaching English: Investigating its Effect on Listening and Speaking Skills. i-manager's Journal on English Language Teaching, Vol. 7 No. 4. https://www.imanagerpublications.com
title: Set of communicative classroom activities embedding 21st century skills in listening and speaking lessons
description: The treatment consisted of activities integrated into regular high school content through which learners practiced speaking and listening via 21st century skills. The article lists the skills as "critical thinking and problem solving, communication and collaboration, interpersonal skills, leadership, and technology literacy". Example activities included "Criticize your book. Imagine your favorite book. Speak about it.", designing questions for school managers about problems, giving group solutions, and imagining future life and jobs. Some activities were done in class, others prepared between sessions, and some filled ten or 15 minutes at the end of class.
requirements: A teacher willing to integrate the activities into the regular high school listening and speaking content across sessions
constraints: Some activities were done as the core of one session and others only in ten or 15 minutes at the end of class
target_learners: female second-grade Iranian high school EFL students
examples: Activities such as criticizing a favorite book, designing questions for managers, discussing a social problem, and imagining future life were used in the experimental class
key_sources: Hamid Ashraf, Fatemeh Ahmadi, Mansooreh Hosseinnia. (2017). Integrating 21st Century Skills into Teaching English: Investigating its Effect on Listening and Speaking Skills. i-manager's Journal on English Language Teaching, Vol. 7 No. 4. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1173769

article_title: Psychological predictors of professional readiness: modeling the effects of preservice teachers' 21st-century skills on self-efficacy and professional attitudes.
citation: Serçe Hüseyin, Aydoğmuş Mevlüt, Şentürk Cihad. (2026). Psychological predictors of professional readiness: modeling the effects of preservice teachers' 21st-century skills on self-efficacy and professional attitudes. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-05039-7
title: Social cognitive theory framing of 21st-century skills as psychological resources for professional readiness
description: The study's conceptual framework is grounded in social cognitive theory, which explains how beliefs and competencies interact with contextual factors to shape motivation and behavior. Within it, 21st-century skills are conceptualized as "competence-based resources that are expected to be positively associated with preservice teachers' teacher self-efficacy and their attitudes toward the teaching profession." Mastery experiences from developing these competencies are treated as a key source of self-efficacy beliefs, which in turn relate to professional attitudes and commitment.
requirements: Measurement of 21st-century skills, teacher self-efficacy, and professional attitudes as distinct validated constructs
constraints: The framework was tested cross-sectionally, so associations rather than causal relationships were examined
target_learners: preservice teachers in teacher education programs
target_learning_goals: 21st-century competencies such as critical thinking, collaboration, problem solving, and digital literacy
examples: The structural model specified 21st-century skills as the exogenous predictor and teacher self-efficacy and attitudes as endogenous outcome variables
key_sources: Serçe Hüseyin, Aydoğmuş Mevlüt, Şentürk Cihad. (2026). Psychological predictors of professional readiness: modeling the effects of preservice teachers' 21st-century skills on self-efficacy and professional attitudes. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-05039-7

article_title: Twenty-one Entrusted Professional Activities in German Dental Education-Day-One Competencies.
citation: Kosić Nejra, Gerhardt‐Szép Susanne. (2025). Twenty‐one Entrusted Professional Activities in German Dental Education—Day‐One Competencies. Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1002/jdd.13931
title: Set of 21 entrustable professional activities for German dental education matched to NKLZ domains
description: A set of 21 EPAs covering all areas currently taught in the German dental graduate program, developed through literature research on EPAs in dental education across Europe, Asia, and the United States, a Delphi round matching each EPA to domains of the National Catalog of Learning Objectives in Dentistry (NKLZ), and a qualitative review by 30 dentists, specialists, and educational researchers. The article states "21 EPAs were chosen, covering all areas currently taught in the dental graduate program", and Figure 1 maps EPAs to NKLZ domains. The set spans history taking, examination, diagnosis, treatment planning, restorative and surgical care, communication, interprofessional collaboration, and scientific and clinical reasoning.
requirements: Alignment with the NKLZ domains, ensured by matching each EPA to the reference document defining learning objectives for dental education in Germany
constraints: The EPA framework created in this study is specific to one institution, adapted from medicine, pharmacy, veterinary medicine, and dentistry examples in the United States, Asia, and Europe to German dental education
target_learners: Dental students and newly graduated dentists in Germany
target_learning_goals: Day‐one clinical competencies across all dental disciplines, including clinical skills, professional behavior, and communication
examples: Each EPA statement was rated on a 6‐point Likert scale by 100 dentists, with qualitative feedback used to suggest modifications
key_sources: Kosić Nejra, Gerhardt‐Szép Susanne. (2025). Twenty‐one Entrusted Professional Activities in German Dental Education—Day‐One Competencies. Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1002/jdd.13931

article_title: Impact of simulated patient-based communication training vs. real patient-based communication training on empathetic behaviour in undergraduate students - a prospective evaluation study.
citation: Britz Vanessa, Sterz Jasmina, Koch Yannik, Schreckenbach Teresa, Stefanescu Maria-Christina, Zinßer Uwe, Verboket Rene Danilo, Sommer Katharina, Ruesseler Miriam. (2024). Impact of simulated patient-based communication training vs. real patient-based communication training on empathetic behaviour in undergraduate students – a prospective evaluation study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05801-8
title: 210-minute peer-taught communication skills lab unit on history taking and informed consent
description: A mandatory communication training unit within a surgical skills lab for third-year medical students, instructing correct medical history taking and structuring of informed consent discussions. "This unit of 210 min duration is held by peer tutors who have been specifically trained beforehand." It combines theoretical parts, role-playing exercises in a hospital setting, and 360° feedback, and focuses on empathetic behaviour and strategies for taboo-afflicted topics. Quality is maintained via tutor manuals, standardised presentations and mandatory tutor training.
requirements: Specifically trained peer tutors, tutor manuals, standardised presentations and mandatory regular tutor training to maintain unit quality
constraints: The study notes individual randomisation was not possible due to curricular integration; students were assigned to groups in advance by the Office of the Dean
examples: By the end of the unit, each student has taken part in at least one history taking training or has led at least one informed consent discussion
key_sources: Britz Vanessa, Sterz Jasmina, Koch Yannik, Schreckenbach Teresa, Stefanescu Maria-Christina, Zinßer Uwe, Verboket Rene Danilo, Sommer Katharina, Ruesseler Miriam. (2024). Impact of simulated patient-based communication training vs. real patient-based communication training on empathetic behaviour in undergraduate students – a prospective evaluation study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05801-8

article_title: Simulation-Based Mastery Learning Improves the Performance of Donning and Doffing of Personal Protective Equipment by Medical Students.
citation: Miller Danielle T. MD, MEd; Pokrajac Nicholas MD; Ngo Jessica MD; Gallegos Moises MD, MPH; Dixon William MD, MSEd; Roszczynialski Kelly N. MD; Ng Kristen MD; Taleghani Nounou MD, PhD; Gisondi Michael A. MD (2022). Simulation-Based Mastery Learning Improves the Performance of Donning and Doffing of Personal Protective Equipment by Medical Students. Western Journal of Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.5811/westjem.2022.2.54748
title: 21-item PPE donning and doffing checklist with a 21/21 mastery Angoff minimum passing standard
description: A previously published 21-item checklist of proper PPE use, "created using PPE guidelines from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and Stanford Health Care Infection Control." One point was awarded per correctly performed item and zero for omitted or incorrect items, with "The MPS was 21/21 items performed correctly, which was determined by a Mastery Angoff standard setting." Seven EM faculty raters achieved 96% percent agreement scoring three standardized videos.
requirements: Rater training (a 30-minute training video plus calibration scoring of standardized videos) and facilitators experienced with the mastery learning curriculum.
constraints: The assessment covered PPE use for airborne precautions only; other PPE donning and doffing variations were not evaluated.
target_learning_goals: Correct donning and doffing of personal protective equipment for airborne precautions
examples: Used as both the baseline and post-test assessment in the SBML sessions, rated by trained EM faculty.
